Welcome
Here at North Baddesley Infant School and Nursery we nurture our children to be the best they can be, encouraging them to be resilient, independent and respectful. We believe in lifelong learning, regularly showing our children that we are all learners and believe that learning changes lives.

pageCache.pageTitle: North Baddesley Infant School - PE and Sport Premium
pageCache.text:
PE and Sport Premium
The government believes that all young people should have the opportunity to live healthy and active lives. A positive experience of sport and physical activity at a young age can build a lifetime habit of participation and is central to meeting the government’s ambitions for a world-class education system.
Physical activity has numerous benefits for children and young people’s physical health, as well as their mental wellbeing (increasing self-esteem and emotional wellbeing and lowering anxiety and depression). Children who are physically active are happier, more resilient and more trusting of their peers. Ensuring that pupils have access to sufficient daily activity can also have wider benefits for children and schools, improving behaviour as well as enhancing academic achievement.
The School Sport and Activity Action Plan sets out the government’s commitment to ensuring that children and young people have access to at least 60 minutes of sport and physical activity per day, with a recommendation of 30 minutes of this delivered during the school day (in line with the Chief Medical Officer's guidelines which recommend an average of at least 60 minutes per day across the week).
The PE and Sport Premium can help primary schools to achieve this aim, providing them with £320m of government funding to make additional and sustainable improvements to the quality of the PE, physical activity and sport offered through their core budgets. It is allocated directly to schools so they have the flexibility to use it in the way that works best for their pupils. The PE and Sport Premium survey highlighted the significant impact which PE and sport has had in many primary schools across England.
Our reports below give details of our PE and Sport Premium Grant and how we allocate the funding.

Special Educational Needs & Disabilities
Children with identified Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) access additional provision and support to help them achieve specific targets to help them progress. These targets are carefully monitored and parents and carers are updated as part of our commitment to working together to support learning.
Occasionally, children need the support of other agencies from outside school and we work very closely with a number of providers in Education, Health and Children’s Services. A full copy of our Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) Policy is available on our Policies page.

pageCache.text:
Pupil Premium
What is pupil premium?
Pupil premium is a sum of money given to schools each year by the government to improve the academic progress of disadvantaged children. The money is intended to directly benefit the children who are eligible, helping to narrow the gap between them and their peers. It can also be called ‘free school meals’. All infants are entitled to free school meals but if you are eligible for pupil premium, you will also receive free school meals in the future.
Who is eligible for pupil premium?
Primary schools are given a pupil premium for:
Check if you are eligible by following this link: Online FSM Application (cloudforedu.org.uk)
How is the pupil premium funding spent?
Schools can choose how to spend their pupil premium money, as they are best placed to identify what would be of most benefit to the children who are eligible.
Some of the ways we spend the money at North Baddesley Infant School include:
See the pupil premium strategy or pupil premium summary for more information.

pageCache.pageTitle: North Baddesley Infant School - Treetops Breakfast and After School Club
pageCache.text:
Treetops Breakfast and After School Club
We have our own breakfast and after school club called Treetops which offers a fun and engaging start and end to our children’s day. Treetops is run by familiar school staff and all school policies and procedures are adopted by the club to offer a consistent extension to the school day.
The club offers a range of activities and is held on the school site. There is a selection of healthy options for breakfast and afternoon snack.
Treetops open at 7:30am and closes at 6:00pm daily.
Session costs from September 2025 are:
Places will be offered in the following order of priority:
If you are interested in registering your child for Treetops provision, please email adminoffice@northbaddesley-inf.hants.sch.uk or phone 02380 412412.
We have many after school clubs available to our children which vary throughout the school year. When an after school club session ends, children attending can then either be collected or join our Treetops provision until 6:00pm; this session after 4:15pm includes a snack.
We also run lots of clubs during the school day, such as RockSteady music, drumming and guitar.
Information about the clubs available during the year will be shared in advance with families via ParentMail.
During the school holidays, we provide numerous daily sessions run by familiar school and nursery staff for our infant and nursery children.
Holiday club runs from 8:30am until 4:30pm and snacks and hot school lunches are included. We offer a wide variety of activities including arts and crafts, cookery, sports and, of course, the hugely popular range of inflatables.
We provide free places to families in receipt of pupil premium through the Holiday Activities and Food (HAF) programme.
The HAF Programme is funded by the Department for Education to provide free engaging activities and nutritious meals to children from reception to year 11 (inclusive) during the school holidays who would normally receive benefit-related free school meal (FSM).
Hampshire County Council delivers Hampshire HAF through the connect4communities programme to all school-aged in receipt of benefits-related FSM who live, or go to school, in areas of Hampshire serviced by Hampshire County Council (this excludes the unitary authorities of Portsmouth and Southampton). You can read more about the connect4communities programme here: Hampshire Holiday Activities and Food (HAF) information | Hampshire County Council.
To book a HAF place at any Hampshire County Council-funded HAF scheme, your child must have a unique HCC HAF booking code. Please visit the connect4communities website for guidance on how to register: Holiday Activities and Food programme (HAF) registration | Health and social care | Hampshire County Council.
Unique codes are directly associated with the eligible child registered with Hampshire County Council. Unique HAF codes cannot, under any circumstances, be shared or used by others to book and / or access childcare places. Misuse of the codes will result in them being withdrawn and children unregistered from the programme.

pageCache.pageTitle: North Baddesley Infant School - Late/Absence Procedures
pageCache.text:
Late/Absence Procedures
Request for Leave of Absence During the School Day
Please complete the Leave of Absence during the School Day form for any absence during the school day and submit to the School Office: adminoffice@northbaddesley-inf.hants.sch.uk
Leave of Absence Request
Leave of Absence Request Form
Please read the code of conduct information and complete the Application Form below to Request Absence for holidays, etc, and submit to the School Office: adminoffice@northbaddesley-inf.hants.sch.uk
Information on Penalty Notices for Non-Attendance at School
It is important children get to school on time as a late start can be unsettling for them. We ask that, if parents and carers know their child will be late for school, they let us know. Any child arriving after 9:00am must be brought directly to the School Office.
Please inform your class teacher or the School Office if anyone different is picking up your child. Please ensure that they have been given your unique password.
Due to legislation, term time holiday requests are not able to be authorised. Requests for extended leave of absence can only be authorised in exceptional circumstances, such as bereavement of an immediate family member. Please read the ‘Information on Penalty Notices for Non-Attendance at School’ information leaflet and complete the ‘Request to Authorise Absence from School due to Exceptional Circumstances’ form (both available from school or above) and submit it to the School Office.
We offer INSET days throughout the year to support families having mini breaks at a more reasonable cost, without impacting on school attendance.

pageCache.pageTitle: North Baddesley Infant School - Our Vision and Core Purpose
pageCache.text:
Our Vision and Core Purpose
At North Baddesley Infant School and Nursery we believe that learning is a life journey, enriched by challenge, reflection and memorable experiences.
By growing together, we create an atmosphere of respect, honesty and growth which gives us the confidence and resilience to be the best we can be. We know that hard work is rewarded with success and, supported by our core values, we are proud to build a future that excites us!
Our core purpose is to improve the life chances of all our children and the wider school community.
This vision is key to supporting our three school values:
We understand that everyone makes mistakes, but at North Baddesley Infant School and Nursery we value these moments as learning opportunities to focus on our children’s social and emotional understanding and development.
Through consistent modelling, teaching and practice, we support our children to recognise and understand their own emotions and to show empathy for others.
Our Vision and Core Purpose

pageCache.pageTitle: North Baddesley Infant School - Teaching and Learning
pageCache.text:
Teaching and Learning
We are proud to work as a team to provide a happy, safe, stimulating and creative environment in which to learn and grow. Central to our ethos is our commitment to value and nurture each child as an individual, to enable them to achieve their best and develop an enthusiasm for lifelong learning which we believe can be life changing. Their efforts, big or small, will be praised and celebrated.
We have nine bright classrooms and a nursery, a spacious hall, Woodlands and Acorns nurture rooms, a sensory room, library and a professional development learning space. Our children access current technology to support their learning, alongside opportunities for music, drama and sport.
Our extensive grounds enable us to use our beautiful Wilson Gardens, wild area and woodland classroom, along with our vegetable patch, for outdoor learning; together with our attractive main playground and multiple play areas, we are extremely fortunate to have countless opportunities for learning and imaginative play.
Our infant children access our extensive playground during their mid-morning and lunch breaks. Our Year One children have their own outside learning area as an extension to their classrooms and our Year R children enjoy exploring their outside learning areas and garden throughout the day.
Our nursery children use their own dedicated outside learning area at all times and also access the main playground and wooded area at times convenient to them.
Teachers provide exciting “hands-on” learning opportunities that challenge thinking. Work is planned to meet the needs of every child and our aim is for pupils to become confident, motivated and enthusiastic learners for life.
Visitors are welcomed into our school and nursery to talk to our children about their expertise in an area of learning and educational trips are organised to further develop and reinforce their experience of a topic. Our Year Two children also enjoy a one night residential at our school before they leave us.
Children with identified Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) access additional provision and support to help them achieve specific targets to help them progress. These targets are carefully monitored and parents and carers are updated as part of our commitment to working together to support learning.
Occasionally, children need the support of other agencies from outside school and we work very closely with several providers in Education, Health and Children’s Services. A full copy of our Special Educational Needs and Disabilities policy is available here.
